title: Even-Odd Position Sum Difference
statement:
You are given an array of `n` integers, each between `-100` and `100`. Positions are numbered starting from `1`, so the first element is at position `1` (odd), the second at position `2` (even), and so on.

Compute the **sum of the elements at even positions minus the sum of the elements at odd positions**, and print the result. The result can be negative.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[1] ... a[n]`.
output_format: Print a single integer: (sum at even positions) - (sum at odd positions).

examples.explanation: Even positions (2 and 4) hold -2 and 3, which sum to 1. Odd positions (1 and 3) hold 5 and 7, which sum to 12. The difference is 1 - 12 = -11.
Even sum is -100, odd sum is 100, and -100 - 100 = -200.
There are no even positions, so the even sum is 0 and the result is 0 - 4 = -4.

hints: You only need one pass through the array and one running total.
Add the value when the (1-based) position is even and subtract it when the position is odd.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]
    print(sum(a[1::2]) - sum(a[0::2]))

main()
